description.text: Applied Optoelectronics, Inc. (the "Company" or "AOI") is a leading, vertically integrated provider of fiber-optic networking products, primarily for four networking end-markets: internet data center, cable television ("CATV"), telecommunications, ("telecom"), and fiber-to-the-home ("FTTH"). We design and manufacture a range of optical communications products at varying levels of integration, from components, subassemblies and modules to complete turn-key equipment. In designing products for our customers, we typically begin with the fundamental building blocks of lasers and laser components. From these foundational products, we design and manufacture a wide range of products to meet our customers’ needs and specifications, and such products differ from each other by their end market, intended use and level of integration. We are primarily focused on the higher-performance segments within all four of our target markets, which increasingly demand faster connectivity and innovation. The four end markets we target are all driven by significant bandwidth demand fueled by the growth of network-connected devices, video traffic, cloud computing and online social networking.

about.description_short: Applied Optoelectronics, Inc. (AOI) is a leading developer and manufacturer of advanced optical and HFC networking products that are the building blocks for AI datacenters, CATV and broadband fiber access networks around the world. AOI supplies this critical infrastructure to tier-one customers across cloud computing, CATV broadband, telecom, and FTTH markets. The company has R&D facilities in Atlanta, GA, and engineering and manufacturing facilities at its corporate headquarters in Sugar Land, TX, as well as in Taipei, Taiwan and Ningbo, China.

analysis_md:
# AAOI — Applied Optoelectronics, Inc.
Pass-1 run, 2026-10-20 (engine release 5.5.0). All figures below are copied from key_numbers.md, dcf_numbers.json, ttm.json, financials_history.csv or fundamentals.json — none are recomputed.

## What it is
Designer and manufacturer of optical networking products (SIC 3674, Semiconductors & Related Devices): high-speed optical transceivers (400G / 800G / 1.6T) for AI data centers, CATV broadband amplifiers and nodes, and telecom / FTTH optics. Vertically integrated — it makes its own InP lasers — with manufacturing in Texas and Taiwan. The business has pivoted decisively to data-center optics: data-center revenue was 56% of the Q2 2026 total, and management guides FY2026 revenue above $1.1B against FY2025 revenue of $455,715,000.

## Owner's earnings
**FY2025 (10-K via EDGAR, from financials_history.csv):** operating cash flow $-174,428,000; capex $179,527,000 (rollup: PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment $179,148,000 + PaymentsToAcquireIntangibleAssets $379,000 — key_numbers.md capex basis FY2025); SBC $11,710,000 (always a real cost).
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2025: $-365,665,000 = $-6.08/share** (key_numbers.md: latest FY OE/share $-6.08; latest FY OE total $-365.7M).
- Maintenance version FY2025 (NI + D&A − min(capex, D&A) − ΔNWC, financials_history.csv oe_maintenance): $-186,761,000 — less negative than the conservative figure only because it caps capex at D&A ($27,696,000) while the company is in a capacity supercycle; the conservative figure is the honest one here and is the one the engine uses.
- OE positive in **0 of the last 5 fiscal years** (key_numbers.md). Per-share OE ran $-0.98 (FY2022), $-0.92 (FY2023), $-3.09 (FY2024), $-6.08 (FY2025) on the filed history, and the operating loss has persisted every year since FY2018.
- Balance sheet (key_numbers.md / dcf_numbers.json): net debt $-172.2M — i.e. net cash — on debt of $33,975,000 against cash of $206,140,000 at FY2025 end, plus lease liabilities of $50,915,000 the engine records separately. The 10-K balance sheet also carries convertible senior notes of $129,829,000 as their own line. The cash position is not earned: it was raised by issuing shares (see DILUTION / SHARE_BASIS_DIVERGENCE below).

**Base used = the engine's normalized base, median of the last 3 FY OE/share: $-3.09/share** (base_source: median_of_last_3_fy_oe_per_share). No TTM pin was used, because the TTM figure is worse, not better (below) — there is no base choice on which this company has positive owner's earnings.

**TTM check (ttm.py through Q2 2026, legs quoted from ttm.json):**
- OCF: FY $-174,428,000 − prior YTD $-116,389,000 + current YTD $-73,781,000 = **TTM $-131,820,000**
- Capex: FY $179,527,000 − prior YTD $54,013,000 + current YTD $335,391,000 = **TTM $460,905,000**
- SBC: FY $11,710,000 − prior YTD $5,726,000 + current YTD $9,254,000 = **TTM $15,238,000**
- Shares (current-YTD weighted diluted): **78,789,000**
- **TTM OE total $-607,963,000 → TTM OE/share $-7.72** — the capacity build is accelerating into 2026 (H1 2026 capex alone was $335,391,000), so the trailing picture deteriorates rather than rescues the FY base.

## Moat: 2/10 — weak
Justification: vertical integration and hyperscaler qualification are real assets, but no durable advantage is evidenced in the returns: ROIC (fundamentals.json roic_proxy) was negative every year FY2020–FY2025 (−13.5%, −16.3%, −21.5%, −17.0%, −29.7%, −7.7%), gross margin ran only 15.1%–30.0% over the last five fiscal years (30.0% in FY2025; 28.9% on fundamentals.json TTM), and the company posted an operating loss in every year FY2018–FY2025.
- FOR: vertical integration — designs and manufactures its own InP lasers and transceivers, easing industry component shortages; qualified 400G/800G supplier at hyperscalers with volume 800G shipments from Q1 2026 and 1.6T orders, with Amazon having issued 7,945,399 warrants in Mar 2025 tied to the relationship; U.S. (Texas) plus Taiwan manufacturing footprint valued by hyperscalers seeking non-China sourcing; CATV franchise with record CATV revenue in Q2 2026 and DOCSIS 4.0 amplifier / QuantumLink wins.
- AGAINST: no returns evidence — ROIC negative every year FY2020–FY2025 and operating losses every year FY2018–FY2025, gross margin only 15–30%; scale disadvantage vs Coherent, Lumentum and Innolight, with transceiver share re-won at each speed generation (400G → 800G → 1.6T); customer concentration in a small number of hyperscalers whose capex cycles set AAOI's revenue; growth funded by shareholders — diluted share count +29.3%/yr and repeated public/ATM equity issuance, so per-share economics lag company-level growth.
- A 2 gives CAP = 4.6 years (key_numbers.md): growth would hold 2 years, then converge to the 2.5% terminal rate over 4.6 years — moot while the base is negative.

## DCF — no supportable scenario table
The final run used moat 2 and the default probabilities 10/25/30/25/10 (probs_used in judgment.json). With a normalized base of $-3.09/share and the F sub-type **no_cash_generation** ("OCF − capex is not positive" on the median window, dcf_numbers.json), the engine returns **Tier F with no scenario IVs and no implied IRR** — score.json scenarios are empty and iv_at_15 / implied_irr are null. That is the correct output, not a gap: a DCF on a negative base would manufacture a number. The engine's growth blend (21.93%: rev CAGR 5y 14.20% · rev CAGR 3y 26.93% · latest rev YoY 82.75%, share-count adjustment −5.00% — key_numbers.md) is reported for the record but drives no tier. **Growth-start sanity check:** the blend sits far below the latest prints (FY2025 revenue +82.75% YoY; Q1 2026 +51% and Q2 2026 +86.3% YoY per the earnings reports; Q3 2026 guided to $255–290M) — normally a start below the latest print needs a written reason; here the reason is that the growth is bought with capex and working capital at negative owner's earnings (TTM capex $460,905,000 against TTM revenue of $595,970,000 in fundamentals.json), so no growth start, however high, produces a positive OE path from a $-3.09 base within the model's construction.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **STALE_FY** (latest FY ended 10 months ago): resolved by the TTM build quoted above — ttm.py through Q2 2026 gives OE/share of $-7.72, worse than the FY median base of $-3.09. No --ttm pin was passed because a pin can only lower the base here; the median base stands and the tier is F on either basis.
- **DILUTION** (share count growing 29.3%/yr): the growth adjustment (−5.00%) is already in the blend. The dilution is **not** SBC: SBC was $11,884,000 (FY2023), $14,790,000 (FY2024), $11,710,000 (FY2025) and $15,238,000 TTM — small and roughly flat. It is primary equity issuance to fund the capacity build: shares outstanding went from 49,393k at Dec 31, 2024 to 74,998k at Dec 31, 2025 (10-K balance sheet) on a 17,052k-share public offering during 2025, then to 84,386k by Jun 30, 2026 after a further 7,776k-share offering in H1 2026 ($1,028,207k); fundamentals.json records TTM share issuance of $1,351,351,000.
- **BASIS_BREAK_SUSPECT** (>60% revenue jump/drop in the last 5 years): the jump is FY2025 revenue +82.75% YoY ($249,365,000 → $455,715,000), and it is **organic** — the AI data-center transceiver ramp (data-center revenue +140.4% YoY in Q2 2026) plus a CATV recovery. No divestiture, large M&A or restatement was found in research, and none is needed to explain the series; the earlier leg of the flag is the slide from $382,329,000 (FY2017) to the $211,565,000–$249,365,000 plateau of FY2021–FY2024 as the legacy business faded. No CAGR straddling a basis break is trusted for a verdict — and none is used, since the negative base ends the DCF before growth inputs matter.
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (>40% in 2023, 2024, 2025): three different mechanics, all identified. **2023:** net income $-56,048,000 vs OCF $-7,929,000 — the 10-K states the net loss excludes non-cash items of $42.1M (D&A $20,427,000 and SBC $11,884,000 are the big addbacks in the CSV). **2024:** net income $-186,733,000 vs OCF $-69,526,000 — the net loss carries a non-recurring charge of $114,232,000 below operating income (the FY2025 earnings release's non-GAAP reconciliation adds back "Non-recurring (income) expense" of $114,232,000 for FY2024; "Other income (expense), net" was $-109,871,000 against an operating loss of $-70,908,000), and the 10-K states the 2024 net loss excludes non-cash items of $153.1M — a non-cash loss year, not a cash-generation year. **2025:** the divergence flips sign — net income $-38,228,000 vs OCF $-174,428,000 — because the ramp consumed working capital: the 10-K attributes 2025 OCF to the $38.2M net loss plus increases in accounts receivable of $127.6M and inventory of $100.7M, partly offset by a $65.5M increase in accounts payable and accruals (CSV delta_nwc $148,533,000). None of the three years gives a cleaner OE base than the OCF-based conservative series used throughout.
- **SHARE_BASIS_DIVERGENCE** (cover-page count 84,569,237 at 2026-08-03 vs latest diluted count 60,183,987, ×1.405, no filed split): resolved — it is **issuance, not a split**. No split ratio is filed; the outstanding count was already 74,998k at Dec 31, 2025 (issuance was back-loaded in 2025, so it barely enters the FY2025 weighted diluted count of 60,183,987) and reached 84,386k by Jun 30, 2026, with the Q2 2026 weighted diluted count at 78,789,000 in ttm.json. The market cap correctly uses the cover-page count: $6.485B (key_numbers.md, basis dei_latest). Consequence: per-share history on the FY2025 weighted basis flatters today's per-share economics — a current holder's claim is spread over ~40% more shares than the FY2025 denominator — which only deepens an already-negative per-share base.

## My thoughts / method range / hurdle price
- The method range here is one-sided: median FY base $-3.09/share, latest FY $-6.08/share, TTM $-7.72/share — every defensible base is negative, so the verdict does not depend on base choice, growth starts or scenario weights. Tier F is robust in a way a marginal F would not be.
- What the $76.68 price (market cap $6.485B) is actually buying is the forward story, and it is a real story: Q2 2026 revenue $191.9M (+86.3% YoY), Q3 2026 guided to $255–290M, FY2026 guided above $1.1B, demand for 800G/1.6T stated to exceed capacity through mid-2027, and a first non-GAAP profit in Q2 2026 ($0.06/share). An owner's-earnings screen cannot underwrite it yet: the same filings show TTM capex of $460,905,000, a working-capital build that keeps OCF negative, and a share count that rose ~40% in eighteen months to pay for it. The question for a buyer is whether the new capacity converts to positive OCF *per share* before the next speed transition or a hyperscaler capex pause — the filings through Q2 2026 do not yet show that conversion.
- Hurdle-clearing price: **none is computable** — IV@15% is null on a negative base (score.json). There is no price at which a negative owner's-earnings stream clears a 15% hurdle inside this model; the name must first print positive conservative OE.

## Final verdict
- **Final tier: F** (tier_by_numbers F, no tier_override; F sub-type no_cash_generation)
- Confidence: **low** (high that historical and TTM owner's earnings are negative — that is filing arithmetic; low on how fast the capacity cycle converts, which is what any future re-score turns on)
- One-liner: AI data-center optics growth story, moat 2/10 — revenue is inflecting (FY2025 +82.8%, Q2 2026 +86.3% YoY, FY2026 guided above $1.1B) but conservative owner's earnings are negative in 0 of the last 5 years on both definitions and worse on TTM (-$7.72/share) as a capex supercycle and working-capital build consume cash; Tier F on this screen — does not clear 15% and no hurdle-clearing price is computable on a negative OE base.
